paper_contract_summary: v1 reports100 candidates per regime, strict fixed-oracle improvement, exact-string uniqueness among improved samples, and novelty against positive SFT D+. Its beneficial TAPE counts are3280/785; augmented counts7153/1789. The requested settings are replace-only and full atomic editing. The exact prompt/validation implementation and D+ strings are unrecovered. v2 explicitly qualifies indel scores as an oracle stress test and corrects the full-action uniqueness denominator78/79 to78/89. It does not supply the missing D+ release in the inspected sections.

source_findings.finding: The public generation CLI has one unrestricted GFP prompt and no action-space or edit-budget argument. It samples100 outputs in batches of10 with persistent RNG seed42.

The CLI parser splits at the first literal closing think delimiter and JSON-loads the entire remaining text. It accepts a dictionary with a string protein field, without checking an edit trajectory or amino-acid alphabet.

Default preprocessing keeps delta >=0, excluding WT unless requested. The paper defines strictly beneficial variants. Default settings cannot identify the exact paper training membership or establish which arguments authors used.

The random-edit augmentation CLI defaults to1000 rows, seed42 and1–3 operations. It writes unscored sequences/actions, permits replacement by the original residue, and supplies no oracle-improvement filter or train/validation partition.
Released ShareGPT construction routes supplied stage tags and emits1-based replacement text for same-length variants; it supplies no complete native D+ manifest.

The published method describes0-based evolving-sequence indices. The released GFP reward implementation instead validates1-based descending edits with insertion offsets, so its parser cannot be silently called identical to the described method.
The public Edit Flows sampling CLI offers length and step parameters but no1–3 atomic-budget or replace-only switch.
The training config references local GFP ShareGPT train/validation files and local output adapters; it does not identify an uploaded exact processed sequence-membership release.

The current public branch is the pinned revision; no tags/releases were returned. Issue1 requests processed datasets/checkpoints and has zero comments. This documents an unresolved artifact request, not proof that no private artifact exists.
